speaker: charlie
text: Now Jamie, our science segment today is all about solving real world problems. Researchers at the University of Amsterdam have just cracked something that's been bugging the fashion industry for ages - how to properly recycle mixed fabric clothing.

speaker: alice
text: This is genuinely exciting stuff Alex. They've developed a process that can separate cotton and polyester using concentrated hydrochloric acid at room temperature. No crazy heating required, and they're getting 75% cotton recovery and 78% polyester recovery.

speaker: charlie
text: The timing's perfect too because new European laws are making fashion brands pay for their own textile waste processing. Suddenly there's a real financial incentive to turn old clothes into new materials instead of just dumping them in landfills. Smart science meeting smart policy.
